question: Should OpenClaw adopt redacted-by-default exec, process, and node-host tool results—with the warning and structured `redacted` signal in this PR—as the permanent agent-runtime security contract?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent and has positive canary proof, but choosing whether existing agents may continue to receive byte-exact secret-shaped command output is a product and security-boundary decision that cannot be safely inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Accept redacted-by-default
options.body: Merge this bounded implementation and treat the warning plus `details.redacted` marker as the supported contract for masked agent-visible output.

options.title: Design an explicit reveal path first
options.body: Keep the PR open while defining a separately authorized, auditable raw-output mechanism rather than preserving implicit raw secret output.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Decline the default-output contract for now and leave the linked security report open for a different approved design.

recommendation.title: Accept redacted-by-default
recommendation.body: Merge this bounded implementation and treat the warning plus `details.redacted` marker as the supported contract for masked agent-visible output.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the shared secret-redaction behavior this PR consumes, making this the closest evidence-backed routing candidate.
